## Additional evidence — the drift is *within* `transition.txt`, not only across the two sources

Hit this from the other side today: I inferred from `rebar transition --help` that `--caused-by`
did not exist, and recorded that as a correction in my report on `1e48-ff69-13f7-4a83`. It was
wrong — the flag is registered and works. Confirming the details for this ticket:

`src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt` is 11 lines and is the whole rendered help. `--caused-by`
is absent from it entirely, while `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:65` documents it.

The part worth adding: **the usage line on line 1 is inconsistent with the same file's own body.**
It lists `--class`, `--reason`, `--force`, `--force=<reason>`, `--output json` — omitting both
`--caused-by` *and* `--ref`, even though `--ref` **is** described on line 11 of that same file. So
line 1 has fallen behind the body it heads, independently of the cross-file drift with
`_commands/transition.py`.

That suggests the fix is not just appending a `--caused-by` line: the usage string should be
checked against the parser (`build_transition` in `_cli/_parsers/core/lifecycle.py`, which is the
real authority — `_parse_flags` delegates straight to it), so all three drifts close together and
a future flag addition cannot reopen this by touching only one of the three places. A test that
asserts every flag the parser registers appears in the rendered help would make it stay closed.

**Why the impact is more than cosmetic.** Undocumented `--caused-by` does not merely hide a
convenience. Per the note I was corrected with, an *absent* `--caused-by` on a bug close re-runs
blame auto-derivation unconditionally, which can attach a **wrong** origin. So an operator who
reads `--help`, concludes the flag does not exist, and closes without it gets a silently
auto-derived culprit rather than a stated one — a wrong `caused_by` edge is worse than none,
because it reads as an established finding. That is a correctness consequence of a help defect,
and may argue for a priority above P3.

Discovered while closing `1e48-ff69-13f7-4a83` (`evileyed-depletive-flycatcher`).
